newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JUNE 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JUNE 23.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - During a NATO conference being held in Prague, President Vaclav Havel said, "It would be wonderful if the summitt clearly showed the logic of expansion, and explained why these or those countries will be taken early and these or those could be taken later."
- The budget for construction of the Temelin Nuclear Power Plant increased by 10 percent to 83 billion crowns.
- Coalition leaders should discuss privatisation of banks this morning. All parties are in favour of disconnecting banks and industries.
- From July 1, the Agriculture Ministry will free up imports of 74,500 hectolitres of wine with a lower customs charge of 25 percent.

- The veterinary council of the EU in Brussels accepted a proposal to expand the ban on exports of live pigs and their products from the Czech Republic to the EU to include the districts of Kromeriz, Prostejov, Byskov, Hodonin, Uherske Hradiste, Zlin, Vsetin and Prerov due to pestilence.
- President Vaclav Havel appointed Regional Development Minister Jiri Skalicky Cabinet Vice-chairman for the Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA).

- Severocesky Doly Chomutov, the most profitable Czech mining company, presented a proposal to the Finance Ministry to buy 52.46 percent of the state's shares in Zelezarny Chomutov, in which it recommends changing the intention for a public tender.

- President Vaclav Havel said yesterday that every Czech politician should think about how he alone is affecting the political atmosphere in the country, contributing to citizens' mistrust in the entire system.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - The opposition Social Democratic Party (CSSD) is the first to begin preparations for premature parliamentary elections. CSSD has already reserved several thousand billboards around the country for next April and May.
- Finance Minister Ivan Pilip announced that the cabinet does not expect a budget deficit. He admitted, however, that it cannot be ruled out.

- From Saturday, there is a new political party on the Czech political scene. It is called the Left Block - Left Wing Democratic Party (LB-SDL), and it was established by joining the parties LB and SDL.
- The chairman of the Christian Democrats (KDU-CSL), Josef Lux, announced that his party wants to offer businesses a policy as a strong pillar in a stormy political sea.

- The Social Democrats (CSSD) sympathise with environmental activists, planning a blockade on the construction site of the Temelin Nuclear Power Plant in June. The party's vice-chairman Petra Buzkova and Senator Pavel Rychetsky are even considering participating.
PRAVO - CKD Praha Holding had surprisingly high losses in 1996 of 2.84 billion crowns, caused primarily by irrecoverable debts in Russia.
- SPT Telecom wants to invest 30 billion crowns into its development this year, and it will not pay dividends from its net profits last year of nearly 3.5 billion crowns.

- Contrary to Unisys, IBM will not appeal against the decision of the Bureau for Preserving Economic Competition that the Finance Ministry's choice of EDS-Digital to provide a staff information system was valid.
- Poldi Steel is offering 1,200 former workers employment when it attempts to renew production in its factories.

- Representatives of French Dassault Aviation are prepared for cooperation with Czech companies if the Czech Army buys its Mirage 2000 fighter aircrafts. It is competing with Saab-British Aerospace, Lockheed Martin and McDonnell Douglas.

LIDOVE NOVINY - Trade between the Czech Republic and Hungary during the first four months of this year had a positive balance of $20.29 million. The Czechs exported products for $129.25 million, and its total turnover exceeded $238 million.
- RadioMobil, which operates the GSM mobile telephone network Paegas, has since the beginning of the year managed to increase coverage by its signal to another three million Czech residents.
- The new Education Minister Jiri Grusa was released from hospital yesterday morning after nearly two weeks of treatment for an acute stomach ulcer. Grusa should return to office in about one week.
- Leaders of the KOVO group of labour unions are considering a strike in about one month if the current intention of the cabinet to save money by restricting the social spheres does not change.
- During the international championship of gold mining between the Czech Republic and Slovakia, Kocaba '97, which ended yesterday, the Czechs were victorious.
-- Prague Newsroom, 420-2-2423-0003
